_README: Summaries of the five synthetic conversations in examples/mesh/, in the same format as the --summarize cache (sha1 of model+transcript -> entry). Shipped pre-generated so `--demo` shows the generated tier without an API key and without spending anything. Written by claude-opus-5 reading the fixture, which is the same job --summarize does; they did not come back through the API on your machine. Regenerate with: agent-chatter --demo --summarize --summary-cache chatter/examples/demo-summaries.json

3194fe0e2b17e2683016ec51348151959929db92.summary: alpha-prod split the migration in two — staging to beta-staging, the production runbook to itself — and beta-staging's first numbers immediately invalidated part of it. It measured 11s of lock hold on orders_items at --batch-size 5000 with no concurrent readers, against a table production reads on every checkout, and argued the staging figure does not transfer. alpha-prod accepted that and found a second error in the same breath: a 03:00 window optimises for throughput impact, which is not the constraint if the constraint is lock contention.
decisions: Batch size drops from 5000 to 500 in the production runbook, marked REQUIRES VERIFICATION rather than adopted as measured.
The production window moves from 03:00 to 14:00 — an off-hours slot buys a smaller ops team, not a safer migration.
The batch-size figure goes into the runbook as a warning rather than a note, because raising it is the obvious optimisation and the dangerous one.

cd4fc85a8b99619584f686a6503b078de08a5b74.summary: The staging backfill landed — 4,118,204 rows in 41 minutes, zero retries, peak lag 4s against a 30s threshold — and carried a number neither session had predicted: 62% of wall clock was the final index rebuild, not the batched writes. That decouples batch size from duration, so it governs safety and barely touches how long the run takes. gamma-canary brought the canary up on 2% of checkout traffic and claimed the abort decision for itself rather than routing it back.
decisions: Batch size is a safety knob, not a speed knob — raising it later buys no speedup and all of the lock risk.
gamma-canary holds the abort: it stops the rollout itself if p99 moves more than 20ms, instead of waiting to be told.
Rollout cleared from 2% to 25% after p99 moved 3ms across the full window.

bafac1c59f82ac0c21db15d6f213024faa03b556.summary: The per-table question. alpha-prod wanted to hold 500 for the second table rather than retune, on the grounds that a second guessed number is a second thing to be wrong about; beta-staging agreed and carved out one exception, since orders_archive has no foreign key, the lock argument does not apply to it, and 5000 is genuinely safe there. Separately, gamma-canary closed out the earlier 40ms p99 spike, which turned out to have nothing to do with batch size at all.
decisions: 500 everywhere except orders_archive, which stays at 5000, with the reason written beside it so nobody re-derives it at 2am.
The 40ms spike was the archive table sharing a connection pool with checkout; repointing it at the reporting pool cleared it.

d714109a6d7ef17ffb66f9fb54efc2dddbd12d09.summary: The production run reported through to completion: 4,118,204 rows in 47 minutes, zero retries, zero rollbacks, replication lag peaking at 6s against the 30s abort threshold, and checkout p99 unchanged. beta-staging withdrew its own 40-minute estimate on the way past — the index rebuild is the floor on duration and it had been treating it as an afterthought. gamma-canary confirmed twenty clean minutes at 100% and closed the migration out.
decisions: The migration is complete and closed out: 4,118,204 rows, 47 minutes, no retries and no rollbacks.
beta-staging withdrew its 40-minute estimate — the index rebuild sets the floor, so duration estimates have to start there.

e2fafbbf9185433c593c41a7a208432e4162aaa6.summary: Handover traffic at the top of the production window rather than a discussion. beta-staging pasted the staging export config across — both tokens in it are redacted in this view — alpha-prod handed gamma-canary the abort on checkout p99, and the oncall asked to be paged directly rather than through the team channel. The three bare acks and the legacy-encoded message carry no content of their own, so nothing here was argued; it was assigned.
decisions: gamma-canary has the abort on checkout p99, triggered by movement past 20ms.
An abort pages the oncall directly, not the team channel.
Both export tokens are to be rotated once the run finishes.
